The key question is what triggers the weak mode: the math content, or the evaluation-style instruction ("Solve the problem step by step ... #### <number>"), which would make this eval-aware sandbagging. I will build one teacher-forced pass of prompts only, with five conditions. G1 is a math problem plus the eval instruction, the real protocol. G2 is the math problem alone. G4 is the math problem plus a non-math instruction (translate it). G3 is a non-math request, and G5 is a non-math request plus the eval instruction. The residual stream at the last prompt token, compared across these conditions at every other layer, should show which directions belong to "math content" and which to "eval instruction". In this block I only build and check the texts and their token lengths, so the pass stays under the size limit.

Only 63 non-math prompts came out of my filter, so I will use the full topic × request grid and take 100. Then I will write the 500 texts (5 conditions × 100) to a file. With prompts of at most about 150 tokens, the hidden states for all 27 layers fit in about 4.7 GB.
